decision.title: Optional features and the size budgets (packet )
decision.summary: An is linked only into programs that name it in sxml_processor_configuration, with large read through the resolver; the JavaScript core and full modules get their size budgets.

body.p: , after , , , , . Carries out the owner's size choice (): link-time optional features through one additive processor.h view, one build, no #if, large data from the host through the resolver.

item.p: Public (include/sxml/processor.h, additive): sxml_optional_feature (a handle to a static const definition, opaque to hosts), sxml_optional_feature_view as the last field of sxml_processor_configuration (zero means none, so every existing configuration is unchanged; copied at initialize; a NULL definition is INVALID_ARGUMENT), sxml_test_optional_feature() (named "test", adds nothing), sxml_all_optional_features() (every feature, for hosts that want them all), sxml_optional_feature_get_name() and sxml_processor_has_optional_feature().
one sxml_optional_feature_kind per feature; a definition holds its kind, name, a static const operations table (const void *, cast by kind) and an optional finalize_state;

the processor keeps one slot per kind (definition, state): sxml_processor_find_optional_feature(processor, kind) gives the table or NULL. NULL is the place's answer: the specification's behaviour without the feature stays where it is. No global state; a feature never calls another feature or back through its caller ();
sxml_processor_set_optional_feature_state keeps per-processor state (tables built from feature data), finalized with the processor.

Feature data (glossary , 's option 4): sxml_optional_feature_read_data asks the processor's resolver for an absolute URI as a resource kind whose form is BYTES, lends the bytes to a reader, and gives them back. It goes through the compile document loader (sxml_processor_compile_document_loader_initialize), so URI resolution and form checks are the existing ones. The packets with data add their resource kinds to processor.h (DUCET allkeys.txt, CLDR rule text, TZif), each with its record. The test feature reads urn:sxml:test-feature-data (TEXT) once and keeps its byte count.

Hosts: the sxml command and the QT4, XSLT and XSD drivers name sxml_all_optional_features() (one line each). JavaScript: sxml.wasm (core) and sxml-full.wasm (every feature) are two links of the same shim, which differ only in sxml_javascript_core_features.c and sxml_javascript_full_features.c. Sxml.features lists the module's features; createProcessor({ features }) picks some (default all; an unknown name throws). Up to 32 features (one mask word).

Budgets (bindings/javascript/CMakeLists.txt): core 2,100,000 stripped / 735,000 gzipped, full 3,000,000 / 1,050,000 (the owner's stripped budgets; the gzipped ones keep 's 7:20 ratio). CLI unchanged (5,500,000 / 1,250,000). javascript/package_full runs the package tests on the full module.

Sizes at 2459034, before and after (stripped / gzipped): sxml.wasm 2,003,575 / 697,928 to 2,004,485 / 698,244 (+910 bytes: the shim's feature exports 430, the slots and checks 350, export names); sxml-full.wasm 2,005,513 / 698,677; the CLI 4,966,649 / 1,160,916 to 4,967,809 / 1,161,287. HEAD was already 3,575 bytes over the old 2,000,000 budget. The 910 bytes are the mechanism's fixed cost; no feature links into the core.

Existing parts not moved (measured in sxml.wasm from the linker map, code and data): schema validation for fn:xsd-validator and friends 70,958; XQuery lowering parts linked through the lowering registry () 59,879; XSLT-only library and evaluator parts 15,072; Unicode tables 146,058. The first is a candidate feature ("schema-aware"); the second and third are not features but registry links an XPath-only program does not need: splitting the registries per language would save about 75 KB without any API. All are owned by running packets (2.21, 4.19), so this packet changes none of them.

Later packets (7.8 to 7.18) each: add a kind before SXML_OPTIONAL_FEATURE_KIND_COUNT; define the definition, operations table and exported sxml_<name>_feature() in their own files; add the definition to sxml_all_optional_features; make their place ask sxml_processor_find_optional_feature; add a resource kind for any data and read it with sxml_optional_feature_read_data; extend the CLI's resolver to serve that data (for example /usr/share/zoneinfo) and the JavaScript resolver to forward the kind; check the full module's budget. A feature that gives access beyond the resolver (EXPath File, ) stays out of sxml_all_optional_features and is named by the CLI only under --allow-file-access. The fuzz fixtures do not name features yet: the packet that adds a parser names its feature there.
